title: Deer and the City's Song
author: Made with Nanik
paragraphs: The tall buildings of the City gleamed like polished stones, catching the sunlight in a hundred different ways. Their busy hum filled the air, a constant rush of tires and voices. In a secret garden nestled between two very tall towers lived Deer. Deer loved the quiet rustle of leaves, but sometimes, a clear, ringing sound would drift from an open window high above the street. It was the sound of a piano playing.

Deer would pause, a little twitch in her ear, and wonder. She knew the notes meant something joyful, like bells mixed with rain.[SCENE_BREAK]Deer wished more than anything to make such a sound herself. One afternoon, after the last piano notes faded, she decided to seek the source. She took a deep breath, stepped carefully out of the quiet garden, and walked down a paved path she had never noticed before.

The path led her past rows of bright flower boxes, until she reached an old, sturdy wooden door, painted green. A small brass sign on the door read: "Music for All."[SCENE_BREAK]Deer tapped her hoof softly. The door opened a crack. A squirrel with spectacles peered out. -Good day, young one,- said the Squirrel. -Good day,- replied Deer. -I heard a wonderful sound. I want to make it too.-
The Squirrel nodded slowly.

-Ah, the piano, yes. But here is the rule: you may try any instrument, but you must keep your hooves steady. No wild thumps. One lost beat, and the music ends for the day.-
Deer promised to be careful. The Squirrel led her to a large room filled with many instruments. In the corner sat a shiny black piano. Deer’s eyes grew wide. She lifted a hoof, then gently lowered it, pressing down on a white key.

A clear, beautiful note rang out. She tried another, and another. It was harder than she thought. Her hooves wanted to dance, but she had to be calm. Once, her hoof slipped, making a loud thud instead of a note. The Squirrel sadly shook his head. -The music ends for today,- he said. Deer felt a pang of disappointment. She had wanted to play all afternoon.[SCENE_BREAK]The next day, Deer returned.

The Squirrel greeted her with a small, knowing smile. -Try the song of the quiet forest first,- he suggested. Deer thought about the rustling leaves, the gentle patter of rain. She pressed the keys, slowly, one by one, imagining the soft sounds of her garden. It was difficult to keep her hooves still, to make each note sing lightly without a clumsy bang.

With each gentle press, she found a little more of the quiet sound she knew so well. It took many patient tries. Then, the Squirrel stepped forward. -Here,- he said, holding out a small, carved wooden ornament, shaped like a tiny deer. -This is for steady hooves. Trade me a song for it.-
Deer took the ornament. It felt smooth and warm in her hoof. She decided to play her very best.

She offered a tune as gentle as a morning breeze. She tapped each key with care, making sure no wild thumps marred the melody. It was a simple tune, but it was all hers.[SCENE_BREAK]The Squirrel smiled. -Very well done, Deer,- he said. -This ornament will remind you always to play with feeling, and not just force.

For every gentle song, new music will bloom.-
Deer carried the smooth wooden ornament carefully as she walked back home, the sounds of the City now seeming to sing along with her.[SCENE_BREAK]Did you like the story? Come back tomorrow, and you will find out what other sounds Deer learned to make.
